country.second_extractor_value: Syria, specifically opposition-controlled areas of Dar'a and Quneitra governorates in southern Syria

sample_size.second_extractor_value: 1,281 households in the 2016 analytical sample and 1,360 in 2017; total complete responses before excluding households without children under five were 1,825 and 1,921
sample_size.where: Abstract; Results—Household survey, pp. 3–4; Tables 1–2, pp. 4 and 8

study_design.second_extractor_value: Quantitative cross-sectional household surveys conducted in two rounds in 2016 and 2017, constituting repeated cross-sectional surveys

effect_estimate.second_extractor_value: FCR >0.1 mg/L increased from 4.1% in 2016 to 27.9% in 2017; WSP programming was associated with FCR >0.1 mg/L (mixed-effects OR 24.16, 95% CI 5.93–98.48); piped-network use declined from 22.0% to 15.3%; reported childhood diarrhea declined from 32.8% to 20.4%
effect_estimate.where: Abstract—Results; Tables 1, 2, and 6, pp. 4, 8, and 10; Discussion, pp. 10–11

risk_of_bias_tool.second_extractor_value: JBI Analytical Cross Sectional Studies checklist is appropriate

mechanism_certainty.second_extractor_value: 1 — documented observational association; the cross-sectional comparison links WSP exposure with FCR but does not directly observe or establish the causal mechanism
mechanism_certainty.where: Methods—Statistical analysis, p. 3; Table 6, p. 10; limitations, p. 11
mechanism_certainty.comment: The authors explicitly state that causation cannot be determined from the cross-sectional surveys.

mechanism_flags.second_extractor_value: fees/financial cost, service_area or territorial access, and regulation/WSP programming are supported; administrative burden and institutional fragmentation are not empirically established as mechanisms
mechanism_flags.where: Background, pp. 2–3; Results, pp. 4–10; Discussion, pp. 10–12
mechanism_flags.comment: Financial burden is an outcome of water purchasing, while institutional fragmentation is contextual and enforcement was not directly measured.
